data.name: Orlagua Republic
data.short_lore: Orlagua is a republic of canal cities whose merchant guilds elect a Ducal Provost from their own council each year. Its coffers buy crossbows, pikes and sellswords rather than risk guild blood. Regency tolls and Salt-road loans bind the guilds, and rival river towns watch for any sign of weakness.

towns.name: Calvenza
towns.blurb: Glassworks on the outer islands; its kilns light the lagoon at night and its glass is sold to every court.

towns.name: Brenzolo
towns.blurb: Salt-fish market where guild factors weigh every catch and quarrel over the price of eels.

towns.name: Orsana Vara
towns.blurb: Mint city of the Republic, where the guild treasury stores its gold behind iron doors.

towns.name: Feltravo
towns.blurb: Felt-and-wool town on the high canal; a legend says its first Provost drowned rather than sign a tariff.

towns.name: Sorvelle
towns.blurb: A town of sluice gates and weirs; whoever controls its locks controls water to three rival cities.

towns.name: Ancaro Ponte
towns.blurb: Bridge-town at the river mouth, toll-house of the Republic and a grudge with the Regency.

castles.name: Gaiazzo
castles.blurb: Lombard hill-fort guarding the river pass, long contested by the Regency's marshals.

castles.name: Torre Sallante
castles.blurb: Tower of salt-merchants; its cellars hold the guild's debts written on cracked wax.

castles.name: Pelagrino
castles.blurb: Chapel-fortress where pilgrims pay tolls to cross; the monks keep the best ledgers in the land.

castles.name: Ostrenga
castles.blurb: Damp stone keep on a marsh island, rented out to mercenary companies by the season.

castles.name: Montorzo
castles.blurb: Hilltop castle whose lords refuse to pay canal tolls and sell their wine to the highest bidder.

castles.name: Fiorvena
castles.blurb: Garden castle with orchards irrigated by a Republic-built aqueduct; the Provost summers here.

castles.name: Dolmare
castles.blurb: Coastal fort at the lagoon mouth; its beacon warns merchant ships of Fen raiders.

castles.name: Scarnara
castles.blurb: Ruined castle whose drowned cellars are said to hold a guild hoard nobody has recovered.

castles.name: Lusiglio
castles.blurb: Border keep on the frontier with the Forest Wardens; its gate-tolls fund half the garrison.

villages.name: Cavedina
villages.blurb: Reed-cutters who sell thatch to every canal city; their feud with Fen boatmen is older than the Republic.

villages.name: Brollo
villages.blurb: Orchard village famed for pear brandy, shipped downriver in barrels stamped with guild seals.

villages.name: Pozzale
villages.blurb: Well-village where water-clerks test every cistern; they swear a curse lies in the deepest one.

villages.name: Remigo
villages.blurb: Oarmakers' village, its ash-trees felled and carved into the rowers of a thousand galleys.

villages.name: Caldoro
villages.blurb: Hot-spring village that sells bathing rights to merchants and heals no one who owes a debt.

villages.name: Sciaretto
villages.blurb: Fishing hamlet whose nets are tied with guild knots; its catch pays the Sorvelle locks.

villages.name: Nevrone
villages.blurb: Snow-fed mill village grinding grain for three cities, always short of millers and honest weights.

villages.name: Gorgola
villages.blurb: A whirlpool village at the river bend; sailors pray here before crossing the Ancaro sluices.

villages.name: Stellaro
villages.blurb: Lamp-makers' village; its oil lamps mark the canal routes and are sold across the Regency.

villages.name: Pescaldo
villages.blurb: Eel-catchers' village; they swear their eels are blessed and pay yearly tithes to the Pelagrino monks.

villages.name: Mantesca
villages.blurb: Dye-works village where cloth is coloured with woad and madder; its runoff tints the river blue.

villages.name: Dorsolo
villages.blurb: Gilded-mud village where prospectors wash silt for flecks of gold; they never share their claims.

villages.name: Ravanelle
villages.blurb: Market-garden village whose radishes and leeks feed Brenzolo's fish-market; a bitter rivalry.

villages.name: Ciotto
villages.blurb: Stone-quarry village whose masons built half the canal bridges; a strike here once froze trade for a year.

villages.name: Bindaro
villages.blurb: Rope-walk village where hemp is spun for every guild galley; each rope is knotted with a guild's name.

villages.name: Ussaglia
villages.blurb: Ferry village at the lagoon edge; ferrymen smuggle salt past the Republic's tolls each night.

villages.name: Valgrana
villages.blurb: Grain-valley village whose harvest pays the Republic's mercenary wages; its lords are sullen and proud.

villages.name: Fosselle
villages.blurb: Moat-hamlet of wattle huts, flooded each spring; its people are proud, poor, and owe no one.

villages.name: Ottavino
villages.blurb: Ledger-village where clerks copy every guild contract by hand; a fire here burned three years of debts.

villages.name: Lunzago
villages.blurb: Moonlit wharf-village where smugglers and Salt-road traders haggle over prices after dark.

villages.name: Zavorrino
villages.blurb: Ballast-village where galleys take on stone before crossing the open lagoon; its quarry is dug to the sea.
